subject: RM_Emberscythe

observed./mnt/d/ClaudeWork/rimmandrake/art_eval/r: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South is a front view: a triangular plated head with two red compound eyes and long curved antennae, two raised raptorial arms whose long curved blades glow orange-red on their inner edges, and four legs splayed low. East is a side profile: a long, raised, plated thorax and head on the right, blades hanging forward and down, and a big rounded abdomen of overlapping plates resting low at the left. North is a rear view: the segmented plated back and abdomen run down the centre, the antennae show above, the blades flank both sides with the same glowing inner edges, and the legs splay out. No face shows on north. All three look similar in size.

Front-on mantis-like creature. The head points down, with two glossy red-orange compound eyes and mandibles. The plates are charcoal with ember-red seams and a grey ash speckle. Thick, scaly, artichoke-like plating covers the body. The raptorial forearms fold up at the shoulders and end in long single curved blades with molten orange cutting edges. Four clawed walking legs splay at the bottom. The cut-out is clean with no ground.

True side profile in a crouch. The heavy, rounded abdomen of overlapping armour plates sits low. The thorax rises to a plated head with a red eye, mouthparts and two swept-back antennae. Two scythe forelimbs hang forward, each a long single curved blade with a glowing orange edge. The mid and hind legs are bent, with clawed feet. Grey ash dust lies on the upper plates. There is no ground or shadow.

Rear view. Stacked chevron dorsal plates, dusted grey with ember seams, run from the neck to a pointed abdomen tip. The antennae curve up beyond the head, and no eyes or face are visible. The scythe arms rise at the shoulders with their blades hanging at both sides, glowing on their inner edges. Four legs splay outward. The cut-out is clean.

Max zoom: the east facing spans roughly 2+ cells and stands much bigger than the vanilla human, a large predator. Normal play (32 px/cell): it reads as a dark crouched insect silhouette with two bright orange curved slashes, clearly bigger than the human and the rat.

subject: RM_Sytheclaw

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale. South: a squat, heavily plated gold creature facing the camera, with a red face, red eyes and red legs ending in hooked dark claws, and its tail curling out to the left. East: a long, low, cat-like stalking profile, gold overlapping plates over a red body and limbs, a long plated tail, and a small beaked head with a red eye. North: the body seen from straight above, with a plated spine down the middle, four red legs splayed out to the sides and a long tail hanging down the canvas. It is much taller on the canvas than the other two facings.
observed.south.png: Front view. The head faces the camera, with two red eyes and a pointed gold-plated snout/crest. The back is mounded with overlapping leaf-shaped gold plates. Red forelegs end in three to four curved talon claws, much like a raptor's or big cat's. The tail sweeps out to the left side. Clean transparent background.
observed.east.png: Side profile in a crouched stalking pose: body low, legs bent, overlapping gold plates from neck to tail tip, red flanks, belly and legs. The forefeet are ordinary clawed paws/talons, not blades. The head is small, plated and slightly beaked, with an open mouth and a red eye. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Overhead dorsal view: a plated spine running from head to tail, the head hidden at the top under the plates, all four legs splayed flat to the sides with claws visible, and a long tail running down to the bottom of the canvas. No face or eyes. This reads as a top-down specimen view, not the rear seen at the game's angled camera.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is about three cells long beside a human, roughly human height at the shoulder or lower, and long and low. At 32 px per cell it reads as a gold-and-red lizard/cat shape, about two to three cells long, clearly apart from the ground.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face head-on with both red eyes toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows no face, but it is an overhead dorsal view with the legs splayed flat, not the rear at the game camera. It is reported under NO_OVERHEAD.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: North is a straight-down top view: the spine runs down the centre, all four legs are splayed symmetrically to the sides, and the tail extends down the canvas.

SAME_SIZE.seen: North is 447 px tall against 151 px for east and 278 px for south. Most of that comes from the overhead layout stretching the whole body length and tail vertically, so it is not a pose; the north body also reads larger than on south.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Plates and palette match across facings, but the north is drawn in a different projection (top-down), so the body does not turn consistently with the game camera.

SIGNATURE.seen: The serrated forelimb blades named in the description are absent on every facing. The forelimbs end in ordinary hooked claws.

ALIEN.seen: The overlapping gold leaf-plates over a red body and the beaked plated head read as an invented creature, not a recoloured pangolin or cat.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 gold overlapping plates, no fur: present. 2 forelimbs as long serrated blades: ABSENT, claws instead. 3 furnace-red underside contrasting with gold: present. 4 very low-slung body: mostly present on east (crouched, low), but south shows a tall mounded back.

STYLE.seen: Painterly shading with a texture on each plate and a clean dark edge. Somewhat polished and illustrative, but not cute or cel-flat.

OURS.seen: Bespoke design; not a vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: Clean transparent cut-out on all three facings; no shadow or ground patch.

SCALE.seen: About three cells long and lower than the human: fits a low-slung pack predator.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a long gold shape with red legs, distinct from the ground.

request.prompt: Three RimWorld creature sprite views of the same animal on a transparent background (south front view, east side view, north rear view), painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, thin dark outline on the silhouette only. All three views use the same angled game camera, the same body scale and nearly the same height, and show the same standing low crouch with the feet on the ground and the legs under the body. The sytheclaw is a low-slung pack predator of the burning plains. Its body is flat, wide and pressed close to the ground, lower than any big cat's stance, with the head carried low and the plated back barely higher than the shoulders. Its back is covered in overlapping dry yellow-gold armour plates, the same dry gold as standing quickgrass, with no fur or mane; the plates are separated by painted shading and subtle colour shifts, not black lines. Its underside, belly edge and inner limbs are a raw furnace red that contrasts sharply with the gold plated upper body. Each forelimb ends in one long, curved, serrated bone blade like a scythe, pale bone in colour with a toothed darker inner edge, held forward and clearly longer than the hind feet. These blades are the most prominent feature of the silhouette and are clearly legible on every view. The hind legs are strong crouched haunches ending in ordinary feet. A tail trails behind. The south view is the front view, eyes toward the viewer, the two scythe blades held forward on either side of the low head. The east view is the side profile, with the blade, the long low back and the tail in one horizontal line. The north view is the rear view, seen from behind: the haunches and hind legs stand on the ground, the plated back rises away from the viewer, the tail trails toward the camera, the eyes are hidden, and the tips of the forward blades show at the sides of the body.
